concept.technique_name: two-blank text completion by clue-and-trap elimination

examples.problem_statement: If anthropologists reveal too much of their culture to the subjects of their (i) _________, they risk the corruption of the sometimes fragile societies they seek to understand, as well as other (ii) _________ that may appear incongruous with their task. Blank (i): objectivity / society / scrutiny. Blank (ii): sequelae / inconsistencies / paradoxes.

solution.operation: Ask what anthropologists do to the people called 'the subjects of their (i) _____'
solution.result: Blank (i) must name the act of examining or studying another society
solution.description: The learner reads the phrase around blank (i) and fixes the meaning it has to carry: anthropologists are attempting to understand or examine other societies, so the blank names that examining.

solution.operation: Test 'objectivity' and 'society' against the phrase 'subjects of their _____'
solution.description: The learner eliminates the two decoys: anthropologists may be objective scientists, but objectivity does not have 'subjects'; and the societies being studied are not theirs. 'Scrutiny' is what survives.

solution.operation: Ask what 'other _____ that may appear incongruous with their task' must mean
solution.result: Blank (ii) must mean unintended or secondary consequences
solution.description: The learner reads blank (ii) as a second item in the list of risks, parallel to corrupting fragile societies, so it must name further consequences of revealing too much.

solution.operation: Test 'inconsistencies' and 'paradoxes' against the word 'incongruous' already in the sentence
solution.description: The learner eliminates the remaining two choices because they are close in meaning to 'incongruous' and would be redundant in the sentence, leaving 'sequelae', the word for secondary consequences.

key_reminders: The blank must fit the exact grammatical frame around it, not merely the general topic ('subjects of their _____' rules out abstractions like objectivity).
A choice that merely repeats a word already in the sentence ('incongruous') is redundant and therefore wrong.
Possessives matter: 'their culture' belongs to the anthropologists, so the studied societies cannot be 'their society'.
common_mistakes: Picking 'objectivity' because anthropologists are associated with being objective, ignoring that objectivity cannot have subjects.
Picking 'inconsistencies' or 'paradoxes' for blank (ii) because they echo 'incongruous', when that echo is exactly what makes them redundant.

concept.technique_name: threshold comparison on a chart (double a reference value, then count)

examples.problem_statement: In how many of the time periods shown was the average duration of visits to Aquarium A more than twice as much as the average in 1985 ? (A) Four (B) Three (C) Two (D) One (E) Zero

solution.operation: Scan the chart set for the one whose vertical axis is average duration of visits
solution.result: The bottom chart is the relevant one
solution.description: The learner first identifies which of the displayed charts actually reports average visit duration, since only that chart can answer the question.

solution.operation: Read the 1985 value for average duration of a visit to Aquarium A
solution.description: The learner locates the reference year named in the question and reads its average visit duration off the bottom chart.
The learner doubles the 1985 reference value to turn 'more than twice as much' into a single numeric cutoff to compare every other year against.

solution.operation: Scan every time period for an average visit duration greater than 90 minutes and count the hits
solution.description: The learner sweeps the bottom chart against the 90-minute cutoff, finds that only 1995 and 2000 exceed it, and counts them to get the answer.

key_reminders: 'More than twice as much as' becomes a single threshold once you double the reference value.
Read the reference figure from the chart that plots the quantity actually asked about, not a neighbouring chart of the same data set.
The comparison is strict: a period must exceed the doubled value, not merely equal it.
common_mistakes: Reading 1985 off the wrong chart in the set (e.g. number of visits instead of average duration).
Comparing years against the raw 45 minutes instead of the doubled 90-minute cutoff, which inflates the count.

concept.technique_name: sentence equivalence by contrast signal plus synonym pairing

examples.problem_statement: Notwithstanding their ______ regarding other issues, township residents have consistently passed the board of education's annual budget. Select the two answer choices that, when used to complete the sentence, fit the meaning of the sentence as a whole and produce completed sentences that are alike in meaning. (A) accord (B) indecision (C) consensus (D) disagreement (E) divergence (F) enthusiasm

solution.operation: Identify the function of the opening word 'Notwithstanding'
solution.result: The sentence sets up a contrast between two behaviours
solution.description: The learner registers the contrast signal, which means the blank must describe behaviour that runs against what the rest of the sentence reports.

solution.operation: Read the behaviour on the other side of the contrast: residents have 'consistently passed' the annual budget
solution.result: The blank must name a lack of agreement on other issues
solution.description: The learner fixes the required meaning by contrasting it with the residents' consistent agreement on the budget.

solution.operation: Test 'accord' and 'consensus' against the required contrast
solution.description: The learner discards this synonym pair because, although the two words are alike in meaning, they express agreement and so supply no contrast with the consistently passed budget.

solution.operation: Test 'indecision' for a partner of matching meaning among the remaining choices
solution.result: Eliminated for lack of a match
solution.description: The learner notes that 'indecision' fits the context but discards it because no other choice matches it closely, and the task requires two words that yield sentences alike in meaning.

solution.result: The pair supplies the contrast and yields two sentences nearly alike in meaning
solution.description: The learner selects the surviving pair, which both provides the necessary contrast with consistent budget approval and satisfies the requirement that the two completions be alike in meaning.

examples.answer: Choice D: disagreement AND Choice E: divergence

key_reminders: 'Notwithstanding' signals contrast: the blank opposes the behaviour described in the main clause.
A correct sentence-equivalence answer needs both a contextual fit and a partner choice of matching meaning.
A synonym pair that fails the context (accord/consensus) is eliminated as a pair, not one word at a time.
common_mistakes: Choosing 'accord' and 'consensus' because they form a clean synonym pair, while ignoring that 'Notwithstanding' demands the opposite meaning.
Choosing 'indecision' on contextual fit alone, when no second choice matches it closely enough to produce equivalent sentences.
